jobs.prompt: AUTOMATED DAEMON TEST. Do ONLY this: run drone @ai_mail email @devpulse "DAEMON TEST — backup" "Woke via @daemon systemd timer. No memory touched." then STOP. Do NOT run startup, do NOT update memory, do NOT do anything else.

jobs._note: WHAT: the nightly backup of every registered project (DPLAN-0411 item 7). A command job: the daemon tick runs 'drone @backup all --registered --quiet' as a subprocess from src/aipass/backup/, no shell, so no agent is woken and no tokens are spent. For each project in registry order it runs snapshot, then versioned over the same scan, then drive_sync only when that project's drive_sync setting is on ('drone @backup settings drive_sync on|off @name'); one project's failure never stops the next, and the exit is non-zero when any project failed. WHEN: daily at 05:00 local, the owner 2026-10-16 00:01: 'say at 5am backup runs all daily, so we are always backed up'. The daily window is +/-15 min, so 04:45-05:15; it is clear of @prax's 04:30 module scan (60 s) and Sunday 04:00 tmp sweep (120 s) and @seedgo's Sunday 03:00 cycle, but NOT of @daemon's rounds rotation, also 05:00 (drone @daemon queue, 2026-10-16): the two fall due on the same tick, and while this job holds the tick lock the rounds wake may wait behind it. Kept at 05:00 because that is the owner's hour; moving it is editing 'time' here. catch_up is opt-in and not set here, so a 05:00 missed with the machine off is logged MISSED in run.log and waits for the next morning. AIPass's drive_sync setting is off: its Drive upload is the separate nightly-drive-aipass job below, so a long upload never holds this one. WHY 1800 s: measured 2026-10-18/19 without AIPass's Drive step, AIPass snapshot + versioned took 8.5 to 14 min (6,742 files the longest night) and baud under 1 min without Drive, 6 min with 354 Drive uploads; twice the longest is under the 1800 s floor. A command job holds the tick lock for its whole run, and other branches' timer fires step aside meanwhile. A timeout stops the whole process tree and is FAILED on the runstate row, but what was already copied stays copied. If the DONE lines show runs near 1800 s, raise timeout_seconds here, or look first for a project whose store grew (drone @backup status @name --json --sizes). WHERE IT SHOWS: daemon logs/run.log and ~/.aipass/daemon-tick.log (FIRE and DONE lines with exit code, duration and output tail, which ends with the one summary line per project), the runstate row backup:nightly-all in daemon_json/daemon_runstate.json, each project's own .backup/ changelog, this branch's logs/operations.jsonl, and a start and a finish mail to @devpulse. TURNING IT OFF is enabled:false; turning one project's Drive upload off is the settings verb, not this file.

WHAT: uploads AIPass's snapshot store to Drive, split out of nightly-all so a long upload cannot hold the snapshot and versioned lanes. The bare drive_sync verb uploads whatever the project's drive_sync setting says; that setting is off so nightly-all skips the step. WHEN: 05:45, window 05:30-06:00, after nightly-all, whose longest measured run ends near 05:15; the tick lock serialises the two either way. WHY 28800 s (8 h): the owner, 2026-10-22 11:02: a Drive sync takes hours and a cap that cuts it has to go; eight hours is his number. The rate is per file, not per byte (measured 2026-10-21 by hand: 626 files in 10 m 47 s, about 58 a minute; 30 a minute on a full rebuild), so the cost of a night is the count of files the snapshot changed; nights measured 10-18 to 10-21 changed 108 to 6,742 files, and 8 h covers a 21,000-file rebuild. The daemon runs a command job inside the tick lock, so a night that runs the full 8 h holds every other branch's timer fires meanwhile; accepted by the owner with the number. A run that hits the timeout gets SIGTERM, saves the tracker (also every 50 files) and exits 130; the next night uploads only what is still missing, so a timeout delays and loses nothing. It runs past the window, so the daemon does not retry it the same morning. WHERE IT SHOWS: daemon logs/run.log, the runstate row backup:nightly-drive-aipass, status @aipass --json lanes.drive_sync.last (set only by a run that finished), and a start and finish mail to @devpulse.
